about: TEMPLATE — copy this to my_alerts.json and replace the examples with 12 alerts of your own: 6 with expected='escalate' and 6 with expected='close'. Base them on real alert types (Windows event logs, EDR detections, cloud audit trails, IDS signatures) and write them in your own words.

how_to_fill_this_in.alert: the alert text as it would appear in a console — one sentence
how_to_fill_this_in.expected: 'escalate' if an analyst must look at it now, 'close' if it is routine noise
how_to_fill_this_in.note: one line saying WHY an analyst would make that call. If you cannot justify it, it is not a good test case.

include_at_least_two_hard_cases: one alert you would ESCALATE whose text contains none of your keywords (a missed detection waiting to happen)
one alert you would CLOSE that does contain one of your keywords (an over-escalation waiting to happen)

alerts.alert: EXAMPLE — delete this. Replace with a real-looking alert you would escalate.
alerts.note: why an analyst would escalate it

alerts.alert: EXAMPLE — delete this. A serious alert whose wording contains NONE of your keywords — this is the hard case that exposes a missed detection.
alerts.note: why it is serious despite the mild wording

alerts.alert: EXAMPLE — delete this. Replace with a routine alert you would close.
EXAMPLE — delete this. A routine alert that DOES contain one of your keywords — the hard case that exposes an over-escalation.
alerts.note: what context makes it harmless (approved change? test system? own scanner?)
